solves: Shows a list of events in order, linked by a connector line, to follow the steps of a process and the state of each one, or the activity history of a record, with who did it and when. It records what happened and does not navigate.
use_when: The steps of a process in order, such as a request and its approval, with the state of each step: use the process type.
The activity history of a record, from the most recent to the oldest, with who did it and when: use the history type, with the dot.
Who did it matters: use the avatar marker. The type of the event matters: use the circle with an icon.
A long history: show the most recent events and end the list with the Show more button.
An event that asks for a next step: turn on the action below its text, such as See details.
While the events load, show the loading state; with no events, show the empty state.
do_not_use_when: To lead the person through steps they click: use nph-stepper.
For a history read in columns (date, who, what): use nph-table.
For the tabs of a view or the place in a hierarchy: use nph-tabs or nph-breadcrumb.
To show how much of a task is done with no named events: use nph-progress.
For a feed that loads on scroll: the timeline loads by the Show more button and takes no role of feed.
For rich content as the whole event: put an nph-card, base or section, in the slot below the text; never a clickable card in an item that has an action.

items.constraint: Property only. The events, in order, as a list of { id, title, description, who, when, datetime, status, marker, icon, avatar, typeLabel, action, actionDisabled }. title is required, already localized. id names the slot of the item and the item in the events; an item without id has no slot, and two items with the same id warn once. description is the line under the title. who and when make the meta line, who first and when after it, and when is the visible text, the date already formatted by the product, with the relative one if the product wants it. datetime is the machine value of when, the datetime of its time element; a when without datetime is plain text and warns once. status is neutral, completed, current, pending, error or warning, neutral by default; only the circle marker has a status, and on a dot or an avatar it is ignored and warned once. marker is dot, circle or avatar; without it the marker follows the type, circle on the process and dot on the history. icon is a core name of nph-icon, read on the neutral circle only: the icon of every other status is fixed, a check for completed, circle-xmark for error and triangle-exclamation for warning, current has a center dot and pending has no glyph. avatar is the photo address of the avatar marker; without it the avatar draws the person icon. typeLabel is hidden text that says the type of the event when the title does not. action is the label of a secondary ghost nph-button below the text; actionDisabled puts only that button under the disabled opacity and fires nothing. An empty list is a mount. A value that is not a list, an item that is not an object or has no title, or a status or marker outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

type.constraint: The Figma property `tipo`. process is the steps of a flow with the state of each one; history is the events of a record. It sets the marker an item takes when it names none, circle on the process and dot on the history, and the aria-current rule, and nothing else: the process and the history share one layout. Reflects so the consumer can style and check it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

label.constraint: The accessible name of the list, already localized, such as Request history. It wins over the aria-label of the host. A list with no label, no aria-label and no labelledBy draws and warns once in development.

aria-label.constraint: The accessible name of the list when label is not given; label wins over it. It is read by a property whose attribute is aria-label, since a property called ariaLabel is the native ARIA reflection of the element.

labelledBy.constraint: Property only. A visible title that names the list, given as an element: an id does not cross the shadow root, so the element becomes the ariaLabelledByElements of the list. It counts as an accessible name, so a list with only a labelledBy does not warn. Given with a label, the labelledBy wins, as the native aria-labelledby does over aria-label. It also names the list while it loads.

has-more.constraint: Shows the ghost Show more button outside the list, after it, aligned to the marker column. The timeline loads nothing: the button fires nph-timeline-more, the product appends the earlier events at the end of items and sets has-more off on the last batch. On with no more-label draws the button with no text and warns once in development. Reflects so the consumer can style and check it.

loading.constraint: Draws skeleton rows in place of the items, even when there are items, with aria-busy true on the list and the hidden word of loading-label written outside the hidden node. The rows are an avatar skeleton and two lines, repeated; the contract gives no number of rows and the code draws three (D-1). On with no loading-label draws and warns once in development. Reflects so the consumer can style and check it.

live.constraint: Says the list gets events without the person acting, such as new events that come in at the start. On, a growth of the list is announced by new-label. Off, nothing is announced but the batch of Show more. On with no new-label warns once in development, since the new events are not announced. Reflects so the consumer can style and check it.

completed-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens a completed item, already localized, such as Completed. It is read by the screen reader and never drawn. A completed item without it draws and warns once in development.

current-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens the current item, already localized, such as Current step. Without it a current item draws and warns once in development.

pending-label.constraint: The visible word that says the item is waiting, already localized, such as Waiting. It opens the meta line of a pending item, before who. Without it a pending item draws and warns once in development.

error-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens an item with an error, already localized, such as Error. Without it an item with an error draws and warns once in development.

warning-label.constraint: The hidden text that opens an item with a warning, already localized, such as Warning. Without it an item with a warning draws and warns once in development.

loading-label.constraint: The word the screen reader hears while the list loads, already localized, such as Loading. The piece writes no word of its own.

more-label.constraint: The text of the Show more button, already localized, such as Show more events.

new-label.constraint: The announcement of new events, already localized, with the marker {count}, such as {count} new events. It is read when the list grows with live on and the person did not ask for it.

loaded-label.constraint: The announcement of the batch that came in after Show more, already localized, with the marker {count}, such as {count} earlier events loaded. It is read whether or not live is on.

empty-heading.constraint: The title of the empty state, already localized, drawn by nph-empty when there are no items and the list is not loading. Without it a list with no items draws nothing and warns once in development.

empty-description.constraint: The description of the empty state, already localized, optional.

nph-timeline-action.constraint: The event the action of an item fires when the person activates it, with detail { index, id }: the position of the item from zero and its id, or null when it has none. It bubbles and is composed. The click is also the native click. A disabled action fires nothing.

nph-timeline-more.constraint: The event Show more fires when the person activates it, with no detail. It bubbles and is composed. The product answers by appending the earlier events at the end of items.

slot-by-id.constraint: A slot named as the id of an item, drawn below its text and its action, for rich content such as an nph-card. The timeline does not style what goes in it, and an empty slot adds no space. An item without id has no slot.

type.choose_when: process for the steps of a flow with the state of each one; history for the events of a record, from the most recent to the oldest.

marker.choose_when: dot for the dense history; circle when the state or the type of the event matters, with the status or an icon; avatar when who did it matters.
do_not_combine_with: a status other than neutral on a dot or an avatar
an icon on a circle that is not neutral

status.choose_when: completed for what is done, current for where the process is, pending for what waits, error for what failed, warning for what needs attention, neutral for an event with no state.
do_not_combine_with: status on a dot or an avatar
more than one current item on the process type

neutral.token: timeline/marker-background, timeline/marker-foreground, timeline/marker-radius, timeline/marker-icon-size, timeline/dot-background, timeline/dot-size, timeline/title-foreground
neutral.changes_for_user: The circle is a tonal fill with the icon of the event in the strong tone; the dot is a small filled circle inside a marker box with no fill.

completed.changes_for_user: A tonal circle with a check.

current.changes_for_user: A tonal circle with a center dot and a stronger title. It has no glyph.

pending.changes_for_user: A hollow circle with a thin outline, a muted title and the waiting word at the start of the meta line. The connector line below it keeps the neutral line color.

error.changes_for_user: A circle in the error tones with a circle-xmark icon and a discreet outline.

warning.changes_for_user: A circle in the warning tones with a triangle-exclamation icon and a discreet outline.

loading.token: timeline/marker-size, timeline/content-gap, timeline/item-gap, timeline/text-gap, the tokens of nph-skeleton
loading.changes_for_user: Skeleton rows take the place of the items, hidden from assistive technology; aria-busy is true and the screen reader hears the loading word.

empty.changes_for_user: nph-empty takes the place of the list, with the title and the description from the context.

business_rules: The timeline records and does not navigate. The item has no interaction state: no hover, pressed, focus, selected or disabled. Its states are status values, one per item, and they do not combine. A disabled action keeps the item as it is.

One tag, with the events in items, a property, and no child element. The ol, its li and aria-current live in one shadow root. Rich content goes in a slot named as the id of the item, which the timeline does not style.

The marker follows the type: circle on the process, dot on the history, unless the item names one. Only the circle has a status; on a dot or an avatar the status is ignored and warned once in development. The icon is read on the neutral circle only.

The connector line is an nph-separator vertical, whose thickness is border/width. It runs from the marker to the end of the item, a timeline/connector-gap away from each, and sits at half of the marker column, a whole pixel, with no transform. The last item has none. The item paints the separator in timeline/connector-border from its own CSS; the pending item writes nothing, so its line stays in color/border. The separator changes nothing.

The text order is the title row, the description, the meta line, the action and the slot. The title row is as tall as the marker, so the title centers on it, and grows with two lines. Title and description wrap with no cut; the item grows and the line follows.

The meta line is who, then when, with a middle dot between them, written by the piece as punctuation. On a pending item the waiting word comes first, then the middle dot and who. The date is a time element with the datetime the product gives.

The status goes in the item text, since the marker is hidden from the screen reader: a hidden text at the start of the title for completed, current, error and warning; the waiting word is visible on pending; neutral has none. The type of the event, when the title does not tell it, is typeLabel, hidden, after the state.

Show more: has-more shows the button after the list. It fires nph-timeline-more. The product appends the earlier events at the end of items and sets has-more off on the last batch. The button keeps the focus while there are more events; on the last batch it goes away and the focus moves to the first new item, a choice of Nephos, which takes tabindex -1 only while it holds the focus. If the focus was not on the button, nothing moves.

The live region is aria-live polite and aria-atomic, outside the list. loaded-label is announced when the list grows after Show more; new-label when it grows with live on and the person asked for nothing. A non-breaking space alternates so the same text reads again. The first load, a shrink and a growth with live off announce nothing.

aria-current step goes on the current item of the process type only, and on one item: with more than one current item the first takes it and the code warns. On the history, an item drawn as current has the current look and no aria-current.

Loading replaces the items, even when there are some: the list has aria-busy true, one li with the hidden loading word outside the hidden node, and skeleton rows hidden from assistive technology. No items and not loading draws nph-empty in place of the list; with no empty-heading nothing is drawn and the code warns.
A short list is valid: one event is one li in the named list, with no connector line. There is no ceiling on the number of items, since a long list ends in Show more.

Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the state texts, the waiting word, the loading word, the labels of Show more and of the announcements, and the title and the description of the empty state. The piece writes only the middle dot, which is punctuation.
There is no transition and no animation, so there is nothing to reduce under reduced motion.
domain_errors: A type outside its list, an items that is not a list, an item that is not an object or has no title, or a status or marker outside its list: the timeline draws nothing and emits console.error in development, one per cause.

A list with no accessible name, an item with a status that has no text for it, a when with no datetime, a status on a dot or an avatar, more than one current item, a repeated id, has-more with no more-label, live with no new-label, loading with no loading-label, or no items with no empty-heading: the timeline draws and warns once in development, since the texts may arrive after the first render.

tokens.marker: timeline/marker-size, timeline/marker-radius, timeline/marker-icon-size, timeline/marker-background, timeline/marker-foreground, timeline/marker-background-primary, timeline/marker-foreground-primary
tokens.thickness: border/width, which the line takes from nph-separator

ai_hints: Use nph-timeline for events in order that record what happened or where a process is; to lead the person through steps they click use nph-stepper, for a history in columns use nph-table, and for how much is done use nph-progress.
Give items in order, each with a title; add who and when for the meta line, and give datetime with every when so the date is a time element.
Choose the type by the content: process for the steps of a flow with the status of each step, history for the events of a record from the most recent to the oldest.
Choose the marker by what matters: the dot for a dense history, the circle with a status or an icon for the state or the type of the event, the avatar for who did it. Only the circle takes a status.
Give the list a label, an aria-label or a labelledBy, and the texts it owes: completed-label, current-label, pending-label, error-label and warning-label for the statuses that appear.
For a long history set has-more with more-label, listen to nph-timeline-more, append the earlier events at the end of items and set has-more off on the last batch; give loaded-label.
For events that arrive without the person acting set live with new-label, with {count}.
Put an action on an item with action, and listen to nph-timeline-action, which carries the index and the id of the item.
Put rich content in the slot named as the id of the item, and use an nph-card, base or section, never a clickable card in an item that has an action.
Set loading with loading-label while the events load, and give empty-heading and empty-description for the list with no events.

accessibility.semantics: An ordered list, ol and li, with a name and no role of its own: the APG has no timeline pattern and the Feed pattern does not apply, since the list loads by Show more and not on scroll. The marker and the connector line are aria-hidden. The status goes in the item text, as a hidden text at the start of the title. The date is a time with datetime. The current item of the process type carries aria-current step. Show more is outside the list, after it. A short aria-live polite region with aria-atomic, outside the list, announces the arrival of events. Loading sets aria-busy true on the list and the skeleton is aria-hidden, with the hidden word outside the hidden node. The empty state is nph-empty in place of the list, with no empty ol left.
accessibility.accessible_name: The list: label, else the aria-label of the host; labelledBy, an element, names it by a visible title. An item: the hidden state text, the hidden type text, the title, the description and the meta line, in that order. The pending item says it is waiting by the visible waiting word. The action is named by its label. Show more is named by more-label.
keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the actions in list order and then to Show more. The item, the marker, the line, the text and the date take no focus.
The arrow keys do nothing: the list is not a composite widget.
Enter and Space are those of the nph-button of the action and of Show more. The item answers no key.
Esc does not apply: nothing opens.
accessibility.focus: The timeline takes no focus of its own. The focus is that of the nph-button, by instance: its border and halo. Show more keeps the focus while there are more events. On the last batch the focus moves to the first new item, which takes tabindex -1 only while it holds it and draws no ring (D-2).
accessibility.contrast: The title, the description and the meta line meet 4.5:1 in both themes and every brand. The glyph of the marker meets 3:1 over its surface. The outline of the pending circle is the sign of the state and meets 3:1 over the background. The marker fill and the connector line are decorative. The outline of the error and warning circles is discreet and stays below 3:1 in light: the icon carries the meaning, and aligning that outline is a foundation question, not a decision of the piece.
accessibility.color_alternative: Each status has its own sign besides color: a check on completed, a center dot and a stronger title on current, a hollow circle and the waiting word on pending, circle-xmark on error and triangle-exclamation on warning. The state is also written in the item text.

invalid_combinations: A type, status or marker outside its list — the timeline draws nothing.
An items that is not a list, or an item that is not an object or has no title — the timeline draws nothing.
A status other than neutral on a dot or an avatar — the status is ignored and warned once.
An icon on a circle that is not neutral — the icon is ignored: the icon of every other status is fixed.
More than one current item on the process type — the first takes aria-current, with a warning.
A clickable nph-card in the slot of an item that has an action
A repeated id — the slot of the second item gets no content, with a warning.
has-more with no more-label, live with no new-label, loading with no loading-label — drawn and warned once.

parents: a page, a panel or a card: the container gives the width
a section with a visible title, which names the list through labelledBy
children: nph-separator, nph-icon, nph-avatar, nph-button, nph-skeleton and nph-empty, drawn by the timeline
nph-card, base or section, slotted by the consumer below the text of an item
appears_in: the progress of a request and its approval
the activity history of a record
the history of a record by person or by type of event

anti_patterns: Using the timeline to lead the person through steps they click: use nph-stepper.
Building a history in columns of date, who and what inside the timeline: use nph-table.
Marking the state by color alone, without the circle, its icon or the center dot.
Leaving the state out of the text: the marker is hidden from the screen reader.
Using the timeline for a feed that loads on scroll, or giving it role feed.
Putting a clickable nph-card in the slot of an item that has an action.
Putting a status on a dot or an avatar.
Leaving the list without a name.
Writing the middle dot into who or when: the piece writes it between them.
